claims.description: `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` crosses from the customer-device zone to `process:web-api`, but its `authentication` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to no verified caller identity, any attacker able to reach the internet-facing `process:web-api` can originate requests that the API treats as coming from a legitimate `process:mobile-app` caller. The attacker can thereby place or manipulate customer-facing requests that the API processes; second-order, the API keeps customer records in `store:user-database` and hands placed orders to `process:sims`, reaching PII, financial data, and order processing. This is conditional on the unverified authentication state, not an assertion that authentication is absent.

Second-order, SIMS writes delivery addresses to `store:delivery-address-flat-file` and sends dispatch notes through `process:fax-gateway`, so the forged API identity can drive fulfillment activity and handling of customer PII. This is conditional on the unknown authentication state.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:web-api-to-sims:order-handover`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium conditional on the unknown authentication value because the attacker needs a prior foothold in `boundary:sokify-internal-systems`, where both endpoints reside. Impact is medium because `process:sims` is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, and accepted orders propagate to the delivery-address file and fax dispatch process.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate API-to-SIMS order handover independently of network location
mitigations.detail: Make `flow:web-api-to-sims:order-handover` use mTLS or short-lived workload tokens and have `process:sims` validate the `process:web-api` identity and token audience on every order.

mitigations.summary: Constrain the Web API identity at SIMS
mitigations.detail: Authorize the verified Web API workload only for the minimum required order-handover operation and reject requests that do not carry a valid order context.

claims.title: Catalogue SQL can be modified in transit if the office-to-API transport is not integrity-protected
claims.description: `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements` crosses from `boundary:marketing-office` into `boundary:sokify-internal-systems`, carries SQL statements that change prices and product copy, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If that unknown resolves to no authenticated transport or message integrity check, an attacker positioned on this path can alter a legitimate spreadsheet macro request before `process:web-api` acts on it. The direct-SQL design means modified price or catalogue-copy instructions arrive in the same form as authorized updates; second-order, the altered catalogue becomes the business data customers browse and order through `process:mobile-app` and `process:web-api`.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown transport-protection attribute: the flow crosses the marketing-office boundary, but an attacker still needs a position on that path. Impact is medium because the flow explicitly changes prices and product copy and is tagged `business-critical-data`, potentially corrupting the customer-facing catalogue.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and encrypt catalogue-update traffic
mitigations.detail: Use mutually authenticated TLS for `flow:catalogue-spreadsheet-to-web-api:sql-statements` or sign each update payload so `process:web-api` rejects modified requests.

mitigations.summary: Replace direct SQL submission with a constrained catalogue API
mitigations.detail: Make `process:catalogue-spreadsheet` submit structured price and copy changes to a dedicated API operation, and have `process:web-api` validate allowed fields, products, and value ranges rather than accepting SQL statements.

rejected_claims.title: On-path attacker can impersonate the Web API to mobile clients
rejected_claims.description: Because `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` uses HTTP with transport encryption stated absent, an attacker able to control or observe the network path between `process:mobile-app` and `process:web-api` can substitute a look-alike Web API. The mobile app has no authenticated server endpoint to verify on this flow, allowing the attacker to impersonate `process:web-api` and collect customer order-placement traffic. The second-order reach includes customer details sent toward the real API and the ability to induce the app to submit orders to the impostor rather than the legitimate service.

verdict.reason: The draft asserts that the mobile app has “no authenticated server endpoint to verify,” but `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` states `authentication` as unknown; absent transport encryption alone does not establish absence of application-level server authentication.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because exploitation requires an attacker position on the boundary-crossing path in `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic`, although its transport encryption is stated absent. Impact is medium because the flow carries customer order-placement traffic and `process:mobile-app` is tagged `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Use authenticated TLS for the mobile API connection
mitigations.detail: Change `flow:mobile-app-to-web-api:api-traffic` to HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ and full certificate-chain validation so `process:mobile-app` verifies the identity of `process:web-api` before sending order traffic.
